Estimate Spatial Markov Transition Dynamics

Source: R/spatial-markov.R
spatial_markov.Rd

Estimates transition matrices conditioned on the class of each unit's spatial lag at the start of the transition period.

Usage

spatial_markov(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  value,
  geometry = NULL,
  geometry_id = NULL,
  listw = NULL,
  nb = NULL,
  k = 5,
  lag_k = k,
  class_method = c("pooled_quantile", "time_quantile", "fixed"),
  zero.policy = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A long data frame or sf object.

id, time, value

Columns identifying spatial unit, time, and value.

geometry

An sf tibble with one row per spatial unit (a single time slice's geography), carrying nb and wt list-columns produced by sfdep::st_contiguity() and sfdep::st_weights(). The preferred input. Its rows are matched to units by the geometry_id column, or by a column with the same name as id, so their order does not matter.

geometry_id

The column of geometry that holds unit ids, when its name differs from id. Its values must match the values of id one to one.

listw

A row-standardized spdep listw object. Accepted for compatibility with prior workflows; use geometry for new code. Its rows are matched to units by id when its region ids are the values of id, as with spdep::poly2nb(x, row.names = x$id), and by position otherwise.

nb

A spdep neighbor list, used only when both geometry and listw are NULL. Converted with spdep::nb2listw(style = "W"). Its rows are matched to units as for listw.

k

Number of value classes.

lag_k

Number of spatial-lag classes.

class_method

Value classification method passed to classify_dynamics().

zero.policy

Passed to spdep lag/weight helpers.

Value

A grd_spatial_markov object.

Matching weights to units

Each row of geometry, listw, or nb describes one unit. The neighbor lists refer to rows by position, so build them after the last filter or reorder of the geography. spatial_markov() matches rows to the units in data by id, and the row order of the weights does not matter. It stops when the weights' ids have missing or duplicated values or do not match the values of id one to one.

When the weights carry no usable ids, rows are matched by position: the first row is taken to be the unit with the smallest id, the second row the next, and so on. This happens when geometry has neither a geometry_id column nor a column named like id, and when the region ids of listw or nb are not the values of id. spatial_markov() warns in that case, because weights in any other row order give units the wrong neighbors without an error. Before griddy 0.2.0, rows were always matched by position.

Examples

panel <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:4, each = 3),
  year = rep(2020:2022, times = 4),
  value = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4, 4, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7)
)

grid <- sf::st_sf(
  id = 1:4,
  geometry = sf::st_make_grid(
    sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = 0, ymin = 0, xmax = 2, ymax = 2)),
    n = c(2, 2)
  )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    nb = sfdep::st_contiguity(geometry),
    wt = sfdep::st_weights(nb)
  )

spatial <- spatial_markov(panel, id, year, value, geometry = grid, k = 2)

spatial
#> <grd_spatial_markov>
#> 2 states, 2 lag states, 8 observed transitions
#> # A tibble: 8 × 8
#>   lag_class from_state to_state transition     n probability lag_lower lag_upper
#>   <ord>     <ord>      <ord>    <chr>      <int>       <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 Q1        Q1         Q1       Q1 -> Q1       2       0.5        2.33      3.67
#> 2 Q1        Q1         Q2       Q1 -> Q2       2       0.5        2.33      3.67
#> 3 Q1        Q2         Q1       Q2 -> Q1       1       0.333      2.33      3.67
#> 4 Q1        Q2         Q2       Q2 -> Q2       2       0.667      2.33      3.67
#> 5 Q2        Q1         Q1       Q1 -> Q1       1       1          3.67      5.33
#> 6 Q2        Q1         Q2       Q1 -> Q2       0       0          3.67      5.33
#> 7 Q2        Q2         Q1       Q2 -> Q1       0      NA          3.67      5.33
#> 8 Q2        Q2         Q2       Q2 -> Q2       0      NA          3.67      5.33
lag_intervals(spatial)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   class lower upper type       
#>   <ord> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>      
#> 1 Q1     2.33  3.67 spatial_lag
#> 2 Q2     3.67  5.33 spatial_lag
transition_matrix(spatial, "count", lag_class = "Q1")
#>    Q1 Q2
#> Q1  2  2
#> Q2  1  2
